subject.title: Add testing framework for cron jobs and skills (dry-run mode)

question: What side-effect boundary should OpenClaw promise for cron and skill dry-runs before implementation begins?
rationale: The request crosses public CLI/Gateway/protocol/config behavior and claims safety around tool calls, external APIs, and message delivery, which automation cannot define safely without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design shared safety contract first
options.body: Define the shared dry-run/mock/read-only contract with the global tool interception work, then implement cron and skill test surfaces against that contract.

options.title: Ship cron-only validation first
options.body: Limit the first change to cron validate/test plumbing that never claims global tool safety, leaving skills and tool interception for separate issues.

options.title: Keep skill testing outside core
options.body: Keep core focused on cron/protocol seams and route skill-specific harness behavior to plugin or ClawHub package workflows unless a missing core API is proven.

recommendation.title: Design shared safety contract first
recommendation.body: Define the shared dry-run/mock/read-only contract with the global tool interception work, then implement cron and skill test surfaces against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the prior keep-open review and appears in feature history across the cron CLI, Gateway, protocol, and refactor surfaces involved in the decision.
